newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay passenger revenue weak in May.
newsitem.headline: Cathay passenger revenue weak in May.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Limited said passenger revenue was weak during May.

In its internal newspaper the airline said May, which is always a weak month for revenue, was no exception "characterised by stagnation and disappointment" in key markets. Hong Kong showed 11 percent growth but fell below target. Japan and North Asia continued to disappoint.
Travellers generally showed a marked reluctance to visit Hong Kong on the eve of the handover, possibly fearing high hotel prices.

The Japanese continued to stay away with a double digit fall in Japanese sales year on year in both yen and Hong Kong dollar terms reflecting substantially reduced numbers of Japanese visitors to the territory.
Korea also showed falling sales with Taiwan the only major market to achieve budget.

A handful of sales territories showed "phenomenal" growth with Malaysia the strongest performing sales territory at 50 percent over budget. India continued to be resurgent showing 20 percent growth along with South Africa.
But strong growth areas were offset by deteriorating performances in Singapore, Australia and Europe all showing sagging sales and sluggish revenue.
Cathay said it expected June to show similar results with strong areas of growth negated by weakness in north Asia and Europe.
